title: Majestic Domain Expansion: Promote to a Bishop
summary: Keep Black’s queen alive until a bishop promotion builds a mating net that can be answered only by a fork.

nodes.question: How can White win without taking the hanging queen?
nodes.explanation: Begin after ...Ka4. White has Kb2/Qe3/Ne4/b7/e2 against Ka4/Qb6. Capturing the apparently free queen would stalemate the black king.

nodes.question: Which promotion preserves the win without enabling stalemate?
nodes.explanation: White Kc2/Nc3/b7/e2 faces Ka3/Qe3. A bishop on b8 will threaten Bd6 mate, while a new queen allows ...Qd2+ and stalemate.

branches.title: Offer the queen, then underpromote and fork
commentary: Begin after ...Ka4. White has Kb2/Qe3/Ne4/b7/e2 against Ka4/Qb6. Capturing the apparently free queen would stalemate the black king.
Kc2 declines the queen and improves the king’s control of b3. White offers Qe3 instead.
Qxe3 captures White’s queen. The illustration shows this stubborn defense, rather than accepting stalemate.
Nc3+ saves the knight with check and controls a2 and a4.
Ka3 is the only legal king escape from the knight check.
b8=B promotes to a bishop. Its Bd6 mating threat avoids the stalemate problem caused by a queen on b8.
Qe6 defends d6. Black’s queen must deal with the mating threat; ordinary safe checks are unavailable in this exact net.
Bd6+ checks along d6-c5-b4-a3 anyway. The queen’s defense is also a decoy.
Qxd6 is forced: it removes the checking bishop but lands on a knight-fork square.
Nb5+ checks Ka3 and attacks Qd6. Black must answer the king check before saving the queen.
Ka4 is the illustrated king retreat; this is not an assertion that it is the only legal reply.
Nxd6 wins the queen. The saved four-piece king/knight/pawn versus king ending is an exact White win; its later conversion is outside this selected branch.
branches.explanation: Nxd6 wins the queen. The saved four-piece king/knight/pawn versus king ending is an exact White win; its later conversion is outside this selected branch.

branches.title: Taking the free queen stalemates
commentary: Begin after ...Ka4. White has Kb2/Qe3/Ne4/b7/e2 against Ka4/Qb6. Capturing the apparently free queen would stalemate the black king.
Qxb6 removes Black’s only movable piece without checking Ka4. Kb2, Ne4 and Qb6 cover every king escape, so the game is immediately stalemated.
branches.explanation: Qxb6 removes Black’s only movable piece without checking Ka4. Kb2, Ne4 and Qb6 cover every king escape, so the game is immediately stalemated.

branches.title: Queen promotion allows the last sacrifice
commentary: Begin after Kc2 Qxe3 Nc3+ Ka3.
b8=Q gives up the win. The new queen helps seal the black king’s escape squares.
Qd2+ offers Black’s final piece with check. This is the illustrated stalemate resource.
Kxd2 captures the queen and stalemates Ka3. Nc3 covers a2/a4; Qb8 covers b2/b3/b4. Black is not in check and has no legal move.
branches.explanation: Kxd2 captures the queen and stalemates Ka3. Nc3 covers a2/a4; Qb8 covers b2/b3/b4. Black is not in check and has no legal move.

branches.title: The queen takes b7 instead
commentary: Begin after ...Ka4. White has Kb2/Qe3/Ne4/b7/e2 against Ka4/Qb6. Capturing the apparently free queen would stalemate the black king.
Kc2 leaves b7 apparently available, but the knight can exploit the alignment of king and queen.
Qxb7 takes the advanced pawn. This is the source’s alternate capture.
Nc5+ checks Ka4 and attacks Qb7, forcing a king reply.
Kb4 is the illustrated retreat from the fork.
Nxb7 removes the queen. White’s remaining e-pawn makes this a checked win, rather than a bare-knight draw.
branches.explanation: Nxb7 removes the queen. White’s remaining e-pawn makes this a checked win, rather than a bare-knight draw.

branches.title: A queen move that does not defend d6
commentary: Compare the source’s queen retreat after the same bishop promotion.
b8=B threatens Bd6 mate without creating the queen-promotion stalemate.
Qh3 does not defend d6 or give check. Black still has a queen, but it cannot prevent the illustrated mating move.
Bd6# checks Ka3 along the diagonal. Nc3 covers a2/a4, Kc2 covers b2/b3, and the bishop controls b4; Black has no escape or useful interposition.
branches.explanation: Bd6# checks Ka3 along the diagonal. Nc3 covers a2/a4, Kc2 covers b2/b3, and the bishop controls b4; Black has no escape or useful interposition.

exercises.answer: Qxb6 is stalemate. Keeping Black’s queen on the board gives Black legal moves while White improves the king and builds a winning net.

exercises.prompt: Why choose a bishop rather than a queen?
exercises.answer: A queen on b8 lets ...Qd2+ force a stalemate after capture. A bishop instead threatens Bd6 mate, and the queen’s defense of d6 leads to a knight fork.

startContext: Begin after ...Ka4 in the saved seven-piece diagram, once White’s queen has captured the black bishop. The earlier eight-piece bishop-defense and queen-offer setup remain source context. This study checks the stalemate refusal, both queen captures, the rare bishop promotion, its mating threat and the forced-queen-decoy knight fork. It does not claim exact verification of the earlier larger setup.
verification_scope: Saved board images reviewed manually. Every encoded intermediate position and endpoint is checked against the tablebase. Selected instructive variations, not an exhaustive tree of all legal defenses.
